content: The process involves an observer moving along a predetermined path and systematically counting occurrences of objects or plants along the path. Simultaneously, the observer measures the distance of each object from the path. This method allows for an estimation of the area covered and provides a model of how detectability increases from a probability of 0 to 1 as the observer approaches the path. By combining these two pieces of information, it is possible to calculate the actual density of the objects being studied. The estimation of the abundance of biological populations, such as terrestrial mammal species, can be achieved using various transect methods. These methods include strip transects, line transects, belt transects, point transects, and curved line transects. Each method offers a different approach to sampling and analyzing population density and distribution. In the context of urban planning, particularly among New Urbanist town planners, the term transect is used to describe the gradation of land use from an urban core to a rural boundary. The general classification of New Urban transects, arranged from the highest to the lowest density, includes the following categories: urban core, urban center, general urban, suburban, rural, and natural.
